questions.q: Time period $T$ of a simple pendulum of length $l$ is given by $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$. If the length is increased by $2 \%$, then an approximate change in the time period is

Given, $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{1}{g}}$
On differentiating w.r.t. $l,$ we get
$\begin{aligned} \frac{d T}{d l} &=\frac{2 \pi}{\sqrt{g}} \cdot \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{I}} \\ \Delta T &=\frac{d T}{d l} \Delta l=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{g} l} \cdot\left(\frac{2 I}{100}\right) \\ &=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{1}{g}} \cdot \frac{1}{100}=\frac{T}{100} \\ \frac{\Delta T}{T} &=\frac{1}{100}=1 \% \end{aligned}$
Hence, approximate change in the time period is $1 \%$.
